sermon.title: A Prophet is Not Without Honor Except... 05/19/2019
sermon.series: Why Jesus Is Important to All Mankind
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer looks at Jesus rejected in Nazareth: they saw only the carpenter’s son and drove the real Jesus out. Only one widow and one leper were helped because only they came. He then teaches being born of water, word and Spirit, and growing from spiritual infant to child, young adult and father.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: A short technical pause in the livestream (17:18) is kept as recorded.

Now Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Syria, was a great and honorable man in the eyes of his master, because by him the LORD had given victory to Syria. He was also a mighty man of valor, but a leper. And the Syrians had gone out on raids, and had brought back captive a young girl from the land of Israel. She waited on Naaman’s wife. Then she said to her mistress, “If only my master were with the prophet who is in Samaria! For he would heal him of his leprosy.”
